subject: Provisional dedicated capacity hold for Flux Labs POC — sizing & fallback plan
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@fluxlabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Provisional dedicated capacity hold for Flux Labs POC — sizing & fallback plan

Samira —

Following our call: Flux Labs is targeting a 12-week POC starting ~Nov 1. High-level ask: provisional dedicated capacity so the POC has predictable latency and throughput. Attached is the POC spec (flux_poc_spec.xlsx) and the runbook we discussed (poc_runbook.md).

Key initial numbers I have from the engineering brief:~
- Baseline inference: ~30 concurrent sessions, 2k tokens/min per session (peak)
- Sizing estimate: 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs (mixed precision) to meet 99th %-ile latency targets with continuous batching and caching enabled
- Preference: US-West region, but willing to accept a mixed-region fallback if that affects availability/cost

Ask for the internal ops check: can we (a) confirm availability across Dedicated pools for Nov 1–Jan 1, (b) propose a soft vs hard hold cadence (what can we guarantee vs best-effort), and (c) surface any suggested fallback model/profile (quantized variant, smaller batch SLO) that reduces hard-guarantee GPU count.

Timeline: Flux prefers an answer by EOD Oct 6 to align procurement and contract terms.

Thanks — please loop Connor if there are infra-level constraints I should surface to the prospect.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Samira Khan <samira.k@fluxlabs.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Provisional dedicated capacity hold for Flux Labs POC — sizing & fallback plan

Rishi / Samira —

Thanks for the spec. A few clarifying items from infra before we commit to a hold:~
1) Run hours: is Flux expecting 24x7 load during the POC window or a steady daytime cadence (e.g., 08:00–20:00 local)? That changes committed node count.
2) Sequence length profile: the spec lists 2k tokens/min peak — is that sustained or burst?
3) Tolerance for mixed profiles: would Flux accept a split guarantee (e.g., 20 guaranteed A100-equivalents + up to 12 best-effort / preemptible capacity) if we put a hard hold on the guaranteed portion and a soft hold on the rest?

Quick inventory note (preliminary): as of a snapshot this morning, Dedicated pools in us-west have ~28 A100-equivalent slots free for Nov 1 onwards, plus ~16 available across us-east dedicated-surge and our quantized-optimized pools. If you need 32 strict guarantees in us-west only we will need to either (a) switch some of the estimate to quantized/vQ profiles which reduce memory footprint, or (b) propose an east-west mix (traffic routing + single-tenant affinity) — both are doable but will require ops configuration and a brief network plan.

If Flux can confirm run-hours and accept a split guarantee, we can propose a two-tier hold: a 20-slot hard hold with contractual guarantees and a 12-slot soft hold that converts to hard within 10 business days if overall capacity doesn't tighten.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

[internal note: will pull formal capacity snapshot & reservation ticket after confirmation]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 15:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Provisional dedicated capacity hold for Flux Labs POC — sizing & fallback plan

Team —

I pulled the capacity snapshot for the requested window. Summary (attached capacity_snapshot_20271005.csv):~
- us-west dedicated pool: 28 A100-equivalent slots free (no current hard holds scheduled for Nov 1–Dec 31)
- us-east dedicated-surge: 16 A100-equivalent slots free (can be configured for affinity if traffic is routed)
- quantized-opt pool (us-west): equivalent of ~24 A100-e slots when using 8-bit quantized profiles (suitable if Flux accepts minor quality delta)

Operational recommendation:~
1) Place a provisional reservation (soft hold) across the three pools to preserve capacity while legal/proc proceeds. Soft hold should be non-binding for 14 days and converts to a hard hold upon signed commitment.
2) Contractual guarantee: offer 20 guaranteed A100-equivalents in us-west (hard hold) + 12 best-effort across quantized-opt and us-east dedicated-surge. That meets the throughput estimate with documented fallback.
3) Route plan: we will enable cross-region KV pre-warm and prefix caching to reduce cold-start spikes should traffic route to us-east.

If approved, I will open the reservation ticket and flag the nodes in our scheduling system; this will cost-center to DL-2027-109.

Attachment stub: capacity_snapshot_20271005.csv (2KB)

— Grace

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@fluxlabs.ai>, Procurement <procurement@fluxlabs.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 08:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Provisional dedicated capacity hold for Flux Labs POC — sizing & fallback plan

Samira / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick turn. To align procurement language with operational reality, here's the proposed approach Redwood can commit to for the Nov 1–Jan 1 POC window (DL-2027-109):

1) Guarantees & Holds: Redwood will set a 20-slot hard hold in us-west (contractually guaranteed) and a 12-slot soft hold across quantized-opt/us-east dedicated-surge that we commit to prioritize for Flux; soft hold can convert to hard within a 10-business-day conversion window if requested.
2) Fallbacks: If there is an unexpected capacity constraint, we will automatically route up to 40% of POC traffic to quantized model variants (8-bit) with documented quality gates; we will notify Flux 24 hours before any forced routing.
3) Operational steps: Grace will create reservation ticket RES-2027-1156 and pre-warm KV caches; Connor will coordinate network affinity routing.
4) Contracting: I'll push a DocuSign for a provisional MSA addendum that includes the hard-hold guarantee and the soft-hold conversion terms. Link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/DOC-9f3a2c-fluxlabs

Samira — please confirm acceptance of the two-tier hold by replying here or signing the DocuSign by Oct 12 so we can finalize scheduling and cost estimates. If Flux needs full hard guarantees for all 32 slots in us-west only, we can evaluate but will need an explicit committed spend addendum (we'll price that separately).

Forwarded-for-context (internal):
> Grace capacity snapshot: us-west 28 free, us-east 16 free, quantized-opt equivalent 24
> Karthik operational note: suggested split guarantee 20/12

— Rishi
